artifacts.summary: Verifies the four rules/contract WORK items and the absorbed hook-predicate work; corrects item (d)'s target from a nonexistent general-implementation-hard-agent.md to context/contracts/recovery.md lines 19-26; evaluates three concurrency-signal candidates for the hook and recommends reusing task-lock.sh session-list's liveness computation; flags that the new predicate must run before the hook's existing clean-tree exemption to avoid being dead code.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's agent system, --hard mode contracts for task types without a dedicated *-implementation-hard-agent.md file (general/meta/markdown) are not silently missing -- they live in shared context/contracts/*.md files loaded via skill-orchestrate's hard-mode contract injection (H1 branch), not per-domain agent files. Before assuming a named hard-mode agent file should exist, check context/contracts/ for the same text.

guard-destructive-git.sh exits 0 immediately on a clean working tree (before any destructive-pattern detector runs), because its whole design targets discarding UNCOMMITTED changes. Any new predicate for a different hazard class (e.g. rewriting already-committed history) must be spliced in BEFORE that clean-tree early-exit or it becomes dead code, since the guarded commands (--amend, non-hard reset) are non-destructive to the working tree and routinely run on a clean tree.

task-lock.sh session-list already emits NDJSON with a two-signal (pid-liveness + heartbeat) 'live' boolean and a task_numbers array per registered agent-system session (specs/.sessions/*.json), computed by session_liveness(). Per context/standards/orchestrator-runtime-files.md this registry is produced but has zero consumers today -- it is a ready-made, already-tested concurrency-liveness primitive for any future hook or script that needs to detect 'is more than one task/session currently active in this repo', rather than re-deriving lock-scanning from scratch.
